packages.label: יִרְאָה וְאֵין סוֹף
packages.label_en: Fear of God and the Infinite
packages.reason: The entire Torah #148 is a single unified teaching about the infinite recursive nature of יִרְאָה (fear of God). The Rebbe's central claim is that יִרְאָה itself is afraid of God — the midah has its own yirah — and so each level of fear contains a higher fear, ascending endlessly. From this he draws the two supporting verses: (1) 'עֵקֶב עֲנָוָה יִרְאַת ה'' — the heel of humility is fear, meaning יִרְאָה is the essential nature and endpoint of עֲנָוָה; (2) 'רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה'' — the beginning of wisdom is fear, meaning יִרְאָה is also the starting-point of חָכְמָה. Both verses show יִרְאָה appearing at a different position relative to its neighboring virtue, which the Rebbe reads as evidence that fear has an infinite depth: it is simultaneously the heel/outcome (עָקֵב) of humility AND the crown/beginning (רֵאשִׁית/עֲטָרָה) of wisdom — positions that cannot coexist unless fear is infinite and transcends fixed hierarchical location. All three concepts — יִרְאָה, עֲנָוָה, and חָכְמָה — are aspects of the same positive domain of divine service. חָכְמָה and עֲנָוָה are the two virtues that meet יִרְאָה from opposite directions (one from above/beginning, one from below/heel), and they are both faces of the same holy reality described by יִרְאָה. The concept of אֵין סוֹף (infinity) is the structural descriptor of how high yirah reaches — it is the qualitative dimension of the package. All nodes are positive/good.
